setupSteps: Pulley height: move the pulley to the highest notch, as high as it goes (StrengthLog). Some guides use shoulder height; FitPlate uses the top for the classic chop.
Attachment: clip on a single D-handle (a rope also works); check the clip is closed.
Weight: pick the lightest plates on the stack; check the pin is fully in.

Stance: stand side-on to the stack with the cable on your right (for a chop that ends on your left), feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, knees slightly bent. Stand about one arm's length plus a step (about 60-90 cm, est.) away so the cable is tight but the weight is not lifted at the start.
Grip: reach up and take the handle with both hands, one stacked over the other, arms long with soft elbows.
Spotter: not needed for light weight.
Pulley height: move the pulley to the lowest notch and clip on the handle.
Stance: stand side-on, feet shoulder-width or slightly wider, cable on your right; squat slightly and take the handle with both hands near the outer knee, arms long.
Weight: lightest plates; the low-to-high version feels heavier, so go lighter than for the chop (est.).
Both versions: switch sides after each set (one set per side counts as one set for each side).

steps.title: Get into position
steps.action: Stand side-on to the cable with feet a little wider than the shoulders, the handle in both hands, arms long (chop: hands above the outer shoulder; lift: hands beside the outer knee).
steps.feel: Steady feet, relaxed shoulders, cable taking up slack.
steps.visualCheck: Front: feet even and wider than the hips, head over the middle of the stance. Side: chest tall, knees soft.

steps.title: Brace the belly
steps.action: Tighten the belly gently as if about to cough; keep ribs down.
steps.feel: Firm belly, no arch in the lower back.
steps.breathing: Breathe in, hold the brace but do not hold the breath.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ribs level with the pelvis, not flared.

steps.title: Lock the arms long
steps.action: Keep your elbows soft and nearly straight; do not pull with the arms.
steps.visualCheck: Front: elbows almost straight, shoulders level.

steps.title: Start the turn from the hips
steps.action: Begin turning your hips and chest together toward the far side; let the back heel pivot.
steps.feel: Sides of the waist working, back foot turning.
steps.visualCheck: Front: hips begin to turn before the arms move.

steps.title: Chop or lift across the body
steps.action: Chop: sweep the handle diagonally down to the opposite knee. Lift: sweep it diagonally up to the opposite shoulder. Arms stay long and the path is diagonal, not up and down.
steps.feel: Obliques and abs squeezing; not the lower back or arms.
steps.visualCheck: Front: the hands travel in a diagonal line across the body; the head turns with the chest.

steps.title: Pause at the end
steps.action: Stop with the hands near the opposite knee (chop) or above the opposite shoulder (lift); do not twist further than the hips and chest can turn together.
steps.feel: A firm squeeze at the side of the waist.
steps.breathing: Out, then start to breathe in.
steps.visualCheck: Front: the front knee stays over the toes, not caving in.

steps.title: Return slowly
steps.action: Reverse the same diagonal path, controlling the cable; do not let it snap the arms back.
steps.visualCheck: Front: smooth return, stack moves without bouncing.

steps.title: Reset and repeat or finish
steps.action: Return to the start with the belly braced; after the last rep, let the weight stack rest and release the handle, then switch sides.
steps.visualCheck: Weight stack is resting before you let go.

commonMistakes.title: Twisting through the lower back
commonMistakes.text: Twisting through the lower back. Why: the lower back has little rotation to give and over-rotating there is a coaching-source warning. Fix: turn the hips and upper back together and shorten the arc.

commonMistakes.title: Pulling with the arms
commonMistakes.text: Pulling with the arms. Why: bending the elbows hard turns it into an arm pull and removes work from the trunk. Fix: lighter weight and long arms.

commonMistakes.title: Going too heavy
commonMistakes.text: Going too heavy. Why: several sources flag too much weight; it leads to swinging, arching and hunching. Fix: use a weight you can return for 3 seconds with a braced trunk.

commonMistakes.title: Planting the back foot
commonMistakes.text: Planting the back foot. Why: a locked back foot sends the twist through the knee. Fix: let the back heel pivot.

commonMistakes.title: Rushing the return
commonMistakes.text: Rushing the return. Why: skips half the benefit and can pull you out of position. Fix: 2 seconds across, 1 pause, 3 seconds back.

commonMistakes.title: Arching the back as the handle rises (low-to-high)
commonMistakes.text: Arching the back as the handle rises (low-to-high). Why: lets the lower back take the load. Fix: brace the belly and finish the lift with the chest and hips, ribs down.

commonMistakes.title: Front knee caving in
commonMistakes.text: Front knee caving in. Why: twists the knee under load. Fix: keep the knee over the toes and let the hips pivot.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: can raise blood pressure briefly. Fix: breathe out as you chop or lift.

commonMistakes.title: Hips fixed while the shoulders whip around
commonMistakes.text: Hips fixed while the shoulders whip around. Why: the turn starts in the wrong place. Fix: lead with the hips.

commonMistakes.title: Doing the same side only
commonMistakes.text: Doing the same side only. Why: uneven trunk work. Fix: equal sets and reps on both sides.

safetyNotes: Loaded twisting: a review of sport-related disc injuries describes rotation, especially when combined with flexion or side bending, as the riskier pattern; a Waterloo thesis reports twist combined with other loads raises injury risk. Keep the weight light, the spine long and braced, and stop if the back hurts.
Knees: a locked back foot twists the knee; let the back heel pivot and keep the front knee over the toes.

Osteoporosis: guidance from a New Jersey council and Mayo Clinic advises avoiding rapid twisting and bending at the waist. This exercise is an avoid for most people with low bone mass or a spine fracture (see table).
Pregnancy and postpartum: the exercise combines rotation and core bracing; evidence not found for the cable chop specifically; ask an obstetrician or pelvic health physiotherapist.
High blood pressure: avoid breath-holding; stop 2-3 reps before failure.
Spotter: not needed. Ask staff to check the first time.
Equipment check: check the handle clip, the stack pin, the pulley height lock and the cable for fraying.
Gym etiquette: wipe the handle, return the attachment, reset the pulley to a neutral height, do not hog the station between sets, ask staff before filming and do not film other members.
